title: Working with fct_revenue
author: instaboard (drafted from catalog evidence)
summary: A first-pass runbook for fct_revenue, drafted from what the catalog already knows rather than from anyone's recording: 1 recorded query on the dataset, 3 direct upstreams, 1 direct downstream. Every step below is derived from catalog evidence and none of it carries the reason the original author would have given. Correct it, then it is a real runbook.

steps.title: Check fct_revenue is healthy before you trust it
steps.instruction: Open fct_revenue in DataHub and read the health badge and the deprecation field before you run anything against it. Right now it has 1 open incident.
steps.why: The catalog is reporting 1 open incident on this dataset today, so a number pulled from it now may be wrong in a way that is invisible downstream.
steps.tips: Owners on record: Priya Patel, Mike Rodriguez.

steps.title: Confirm orders loaded first
steps.instruction: Check orders, which feeds fct_revenue, has today's data before you read anything downstream of it.
steps.why: DataHub records orders as a direct upstream of fct_revenue. A partial load there produces a plausible-looking but short number here, which is the failure mode that gets noticed last.

steps.title: Confirm refunds loaded first
steps.instruction: Check refunds, which feeds fct_revenue, has today's data before you read anything downstream of it.
steps.why: DataHub records refunds as a direct upstream of fct_revenue. A partial load there produces a plausible-looking but short number here, which is the failure mode that gets noticed last.

steps.title: Net revenue by customer country (last 90 days)
steps.instruction: Run this against fct_revenue. It is a query the catalog has on record for this table, not a reconstruction.
steps.why: This is what people actually run here — the catalog has it recorded against this dataset. Reproducing an existing query is how you get a number that matches the one everyone else quotes.
steps.sql:
SELECT c.country, SUM(r.net_amount_usd) AS net_revenue
FROM analytics.marts.fct_revenue r
JOIN analytics.marts.dim_customers c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
WHERE r.revenue_date >= DATEADD(day, -90, CURRENT_DATE)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

steps.title: Know who breaks if this changes
steps.instruction: Before changing anything about fct_revenue, check its downstream lineage in DataHub. Today that is mrr_monthly.
steps.why: DataHub records 1 dataset depending on this one. The people to warn are the owners of those, not the owners of this.

draftBasis: glossary terms: Gross Merchandise Value, Monthly Recurring Revenue
